title: Roots of the Willow
author: Joseph Lim
summary: A grandfather visits his grandson’s grave and finds the willow he always rests beneath has disappeared.
excerpt: Each visit, I’d rest beneath its long, curtain-like branches that carried its own grief beside me.
note: Lim gives grief a physical place to settle. The missing willow puts a crack in a familiar ritual, and that small change makes room for a much stranger story about memory.

title: Watercolor
author: Alicia Christensen
summary: Red and blue trace the changing feelings of a speaker looking back on a romance.
excerpt:
Watercolor strokes,
connecting constellations,
written in the sky;
I was the sole reflection in your eye.
note: Watch how Christensen returns to the same colors. They carry a different feeling each time, so the poem can show how much the speaker has changed without stopping to explain it.

title: Chocolate Milk
author: GiGi Shallenberger
summary: A visit home from college finds a younger brother, a house full of noise, and a very particular favorite drink.
excerpt: He revels in noise. It is four in the afternoon.
note: Shallenberger lets ordinary details carry the tenderness of this essay. A couch, a video game, and a specific kind of chocolate milk show what it means to pay attention to someone you love.
